memory_candidates: When restating a saturation-style inductive invariant over a quotient map (rep : World -> World) for a tableau-completeness proof, a field that pulls back the raw numeric world order through rep (rep w <= rep w') is not automatically a valid load-bearing invariant even if it type-checks/elaborates cleanly: rep must be shown MONOTONE in the sense the proof needs (w <= w' -> rep w <= rep w'), or every plain-to-Q lifting site will hit a counterexample where a witness world is independently, later mapped to an unrelated representative. Prefer routing the ordering conjunct through the same reachability/accessibility relation already used for the accessibility companion invariant (if one exists), since accessibility-based orders have a natural monotonicity argument (common-ancestor comparability in a tree) that raw numeric quotient orders lack.

A plan's own scope hypothesis claiming a downstream extraction step is a 'one-line substitution' of an earlier phase's additively-landed lemma should be verified by actually attempting the substitution and reading the type-mismatch error, before trusting the estimate -- Phase 5's Q-predicates here type-checked as standalone additive declarations but had not yet been exercised in a real discharge, and doing so revealed the shape itself needed revision, not just a substitution.
